assessor: RTS implementation preflight — Official Docs Intake + Claim Extraction Adapter v1
rationale: I is an upstream documentation intake boundary only. Network access is bounded to HTTPS official-host allowlists, redirects are revalidated, fetch count/bytes/time are capped, HTML is normalized without executing scripts, and emitted claims are exact anchors copied from normalized source text. Ambiguous contract-like chunks remain visible in extraction audit. Output is validated by H and grants no runtime/profile/promotion authority.
affected_boundaries: coverage audit and H bundle emission
existing_assumptions: H validates transition-evidence-bundle/v1 and keeps docs claims UNVERIFIED.
Only OFFICIAL evidence can establish H transition severity.
F/G remain separately bounded and approval-controlled.
No external documentation creates execution authority or Canon by itself.

data_migration.notes: No existing H bundles, profiles, memory, FREEZER history, runtime router, or provider credentials are mutated.

external_interfaces: provider + generation + query terms intake request
HTTPS GET to explicit provider official hosts only
approval_changes: none; I output grants no execution/profile-application/promotion authority
provider OFFICIAL trust derives from configured provider allowlist, not page self-assertion
hidden_dependencies: redirect final host must remain allowlisted
download and normalized text size must remain bounded
document_id must remain stable across generations for H residual comparison
claim anchors must exist byte-for-byte in normalized source content
contract-like but unclassified chunks must remain auditable rather than silently discarded
rollback_boundary: Drop the I branch or revert official_docs_intake files and FRZ-000019 append-only versions; A-H remain untouched.
completion_conditions: OpenAI, Anthropic and Google built-in provider policies exist with bounded official hosts/seeds
non-HTTPS or non-allowlisted URLs fail closed
redirect to non-allowlisted host fails closed
fetch count, content bytes and normalized text size are capped
script/style content is not executed or treated as visible document text
claim candidates use exact anchors present in normalized source text
obvious context/reasoning/tool/cache/delegation/limit/pricing/deprecation signals map to H areas/kinds conservatively
novel contract-like text is surfaced in coverage audit instead of silently disappearing
partial fetch/extraction failures prevent READY status while preserving completed evidence
emitted H bundle passes H validate_bundle
all I outputs remain non-authorizing and docs claims remain hypotheses
A-I regressions and FREEZER verify pass
risks: lexical extraction is intentionally conservative and may over-route ambiguous changes to review
provider index formats can evolve and require adapter updates
some JS-heavy docs may not expose useful server-rendered text; these must fail/review rather than fabricate coverage
v1 discovers within bounded configured indexes/seeds and is not a general web crawler
